finding: Hypothesis paper proposing competition between lymphocytes and skeletal muscle for glutathione precursors as a cause of fatigue; no new data.

Claims low-level coagulation activation (fibrinogen, F1+2, TAT, soluble fibrin, platelet activation) with anti-B2GPI antibodies and classifies CFS/FM as an antiphospholipid-type syndrome; no numbers given.
note: No data or controls in abstract; atlas reports routine coagulation markers generally normal

finding: Serum TNF-alpha significantly higher in CFS than non-CFS controls (P<0.0001).
In 23 severely ill patients followed about 4 years, 13 stayed severe, 9 improved but still met 1994 criteria, 1 recovered; duration, onset mode, psychiatric status did not predict outcome.
Perfectionism scores did not correlate with fatigue, anxiety or depression; other-oriented perfectionism was lower in CFS (p=0.0019).
Describes disease-management and coping approaches observed in a support group.
Thirty minutes of light intermittent treadmill walking did not change disability, symptoms or mood up to 7 days later, and physiological responses were normal.
note: Very small, no control group, light exercise only

finding: Title only: frequency of mercury intolerance in CFS patients versus controls; no abstract.
DHEA and DHEA-S lower in CFS than healthy controls; cortisol and 17-OH-progesterone did not differ.
note: Cortisol did not differ, unlike the atlas finding; androgen result likely age-confounded

n: CFS and healthy volunteers, n not stated
finding: Delta-ACTH response to oCRH was attenuated in CFS (21.0 vs 57.8 ng/L); adding DDAVP augmented the response and normalised it in CFS.
note: Challenge test, not a treatment trial

finding: 2-5A synthetase (2.2-38.7 fold) and PKR (1.3-13.5 fold) activity raised in leukocytes versus healthy background in both groups.
note: Groups selected by viral genome status; no matched healthy group in abstract

finding: Interview study of life events and infections in the year before CFS onset versus a non-specific life crisis period; fatigue intensity differed 4-10 months before onset.
Red-cell enzyme activities for B vitamins were lower in CFS (AST 2.84 vs 4.61 U/g Hb, P<0.001; GTR and TK also lower) with unchanged activation ratios.
note: Small; preliminary evidence of lower functional B vitamin status

finding: CFS patients scored lower on extroversion and higher on neuroticism than controls, interpreted as reaction to illness.
Patent claiming that Mycoplasma genus/species load in PBMC or anti-M. fermentans antibodies indicate CFS/fibromyalgia.
US Social Security ruling on evaluating disability claims involving CFS.
PCR for HHV6, HHV7, EBV and CMV in PBMC and EBV/HHV6 serology showed no significant differences between CFS and matched controls.
note: Double-blind; n not given in abstract

finding: Stepwise wheat-free diet, supplements, homeopathy and psychotherapy: 70% of completers reported benefit.
CFS patients showed impaired sustained-attention performance that worsened further with acute fatigue over the test session.
During 45-min tilt, CFS had higher heart rate and smaller stroke volume; frequency of positive tilt did not differ (11 vs 12).
note: Neurally mediated hypotension rate similar to controls

finding: Interviews of overseas development workers with CFS: multiple perceived causes, difficulty obtaining a diagnosis, coping strategies.
After exhaustive treadmill test, VO2peak was similar, fatigue was higher at 24 h, but immune cell and cytokine responses did not differ from sedentary controls.

40% of 75 CFS patients had orthostatic intolerance on 80-degree tilt (16 neurally mediated syncope, 7 tachycardia, 6 mixed) versus 8/48 controls with syncope; OI subgroup had shorter illness and more subacute onset.
note: Unselected clinic patients; Valsalva and deep-breathing responses normal

finding: Spontaneous, PHA- and LPS-induced IL-6 production by lymphocytes and monocytes was higher when patients felt fatigued than when rested; exercise-induced fatigue did not change IL-6.
note: Small, n not given; within-patient symptom-state comparison

finding: Serum enteroviral 5'NTR sequences in CFS patients grouped within the coxsackie/echovirus group, though some were 10-13% divergent from known enteroviruses.
note: PCR only, no controls in abstract; truncated

finding: No difference in mood or perceived stress between patients with and without social support; verbal emotional support better predicted mental health.
Open-label crossover trial of interferon-alpha in Oxford-criteria CFS, testing earlier claim of benefit in Coxsackie IgM-positive patients; 25 had immediate treatment.
Basal DHEA was normal but the DHEA response to IV ACTH was blunted in CFS.

No immune differences in civilian CFS; Gulf War veterans with CFS had more total T cells and MHC II+ T cells, fewer NK cells and higher IL-2, IL-10, IFN-gamma and TNF-alpha mRNA than veteran controls.
note: Civilians no difference; Gulf War subgroup only; n not given

finding: Of 94 idiopathic fatigue patients, 48 met 1988 CFS criteria, 20 only 1994 criteria, 26 neither; 1994-only cases less often had acute onset or infectious signs.
EQ-5D and SF-36 strongly correlated in CFS; EQ-5D overstates disability for mobility and self-care.
All CFS members of two family clusters had Borna disease virus antibodies and/or BDV p24 RNA in PBMC; healthy members were largely negative.
note: Two families only; BDV link not established; small

finding: In a nurse sample, functional impairment and lower quality of life tracked fatigue severity and psychiatric diagnosis.
Structural equation model: somatic attribution lowered activity, which raised fatigue; sense of control and symptom focus directly affected fatigue; model fit CFS but not MS.
Mycoplasma genus DNA in PBMC found in 52% of CFS vs 14% of controls and M. fermentans in 34% vs 8% (P<0.0001), with higher copy numbers.
note: PCR; not independently replicated in later work as far as the atlas shows

finding: CSF substance P was within normal range in 15 CFS patients, unlike fibromyalgia.
Morning and evening cortisol and ACTH did not differ significantly, but the diurnal change in cortisol was smaller in CFS (p<0.05).
Chalder fatigue scale had four factors; physical-fatigue factor correlated inversely with grip strength, peak VO2 and work capacity.
L-arginine and a NO donor raised NK activity in healthy controls but not in CFS patients; iNOS transcripts did not differ.
CFS psychiatric patients reported more lifetime IBS, infectious mononucleosis-like syndromes and herpes than controls, and poorer pre-onset physical health.
PBMC beta-endorphin concentration was significantly lower in CFS.
13 of 18 patients had abnormal HMPAO SPET perfusion while 15 of 18 had normal FDG glucose metabolism, showing discordance between perfusion and metabolism.
Nasal lavage markers of vascular permeability, gland secretion and eosinophil/neutrophil degranulation did not differ between nonallergic FM/CFS and normal subjects.
Patent for a cellular immunotherapy using expanded cytokine-producing lymph-node cells from patients.

n: 51 CFS vs 34 normal vs 27 AR vs 17 rheum
finding: Allergy skin tests were positive in 35% of CFS vs 44% of normals (ns); 83%/76% of skin-test positive/negative CFS had rhinitis complaints vs 23% of normals; 46% of CFS had nonallergic rhinitis.
After treadmill exercise, CFS patients declined more than healthy controls on focused (p=0.02) and sustained (p=0.001) attention, and more than depressed patients on focused attention (p=0.03).
CFS and Addison's patients differed in illness identity, time line, control and consequences beliefs; correlation patterns similar.
Multiplex PCR found Mycoplasma genus DNA in PBMC of 52% of CFS vs 15% of healthy; M. fermentans 32% vs 8%, M. hominis 9% vs 3%, M. penetrans 6% vs 2%.
note: Same group as earlier PCR report; not confirmed by unbiased sequencing

finding: Women with CFS self-reported more gynecologic complications, irregular cycles, amenorrhea, and PCOS, hirsutism and ovarian cysts, but less premenstrual symptomatology.
note: Self-report; controls were outpatients for non-gynecologic conditions

finding: After tilt, heart rate was higher in CFS (88.9 vs 77.9 bpm, P<0.01) and low-frequency power higher (0.603 vs 0.428, P=0.02); parasympathetic tests normal; read as sympathetic overactivity.
News item on an Alberta court ruling and Quebec physician guidelines recognising CFS.
Point prevalence of CFS in a Japanese community sample was 1.5% (95% CI 0.4-5.2%), 2 cases; none met 1989 CDC criteria.
CFS patients had poorer attentional span and working memory, divided attention and verbal learning; focused attention was not impaired.
Estimated CFS prevalence among nurses was 1,088 per 100,000.
Legal commentary on an Alberta court case recognising CFS.
In 15 women with CFS in primary care, 60% reported improvement or recovery; improvement linked to social support, lower depressive symptoms and physician validation.
After exhaustive treadmill exercise, CFS patients scored lower than sedentary controls on SDMT, Stroop word and color tests immediately and 24 h later.

n: 71 CFS vs 65 controls vs 23 MS vs 21 MDD
finding: Of 18 immune variables only IgG1 and IgG3 differed in CFS versus controls, and the subclass deficiency was lowest in CFS with axis-I disorder and lost significance once MS and depression were included.
Review comparing post-polio fatigue and CFS (attention deficits, brain lesions, HPA activation, prolactin, EEG slowing) with a dopamine-replacement hypothesis.
FDG-PET showed hypometabolism in right mediofrontal cortex (P=0.010) and brainstem (P=0.013) versus controls; depressed patients had frontal hypometabolism with normal brainstem.
CFS patients showed winter worsening of mood, energy and sleep; 37% of 73 consistent raters had high seasonality scores.
Multidisciplinary programme with CBT and structured activity: of 51 treated patients 31 returned to gainful employment (abstract truncated); compared with untreated controls.
Self-efficacy predicted CFS symptoms beyond demographics and distress.

n: 18 CFS vs 11 normal vs 14 allergic vs 12 depression
finding: PBMC TNF-alpha was raised in CFS (50.1 pg) and allergic subjects (41.6) versus normals (13.1); most CFS subjects were allergic and psychological profile split the CFS group.
13 of 16 adolescents with CFS fainted on 80-degree tilt, and heart rate variability indices were strikingly lower than in syncope patients and controls.
Interviews over 3 years described role constriction and job-loss risk when CFS symptoms collide with work demands.
HAD scale at cut-off 9/10 was a valid screen for anxiety and depression in CFS; MOS mental health scale gave too many false positives.
CFS patients had smaller left ventricular end-systolic and diastolic dimensions, lower LV mass and smaller carotid diameters, interpreted by authors as physical and cardiovascular deconditioning.
note: Large; authors read the small heart as deconditioning, a reading the atlas disputes

finding: Review authors preferentially cited literature from their own discipline and country.
In a CBT versus relaxation trial, physical illness attributions did not predict outcome; change in exercise-avoidance beliefs was associated with improvement.
NK cytotoxicity was lower in 8 affected family members than controls (P=0.006) with normal NK cell counts; low activity also in 4/12 unaffected relatives.
Illness representations (serious, uncontrollable) predicted passive coping and worse physical and social functioning.
After a maximal treadmill test, accelerometer activity fell significantly in CFS women (largest on days 12-14), with longer waking day and more rests, later than self-report suggested.
Home polysomnography showed more brief and longer awakenings in CFS teenagers than matched controls.
Step exercise raised neutrophils 33% and lactoferrin 27% in all women, with no exaggerated neutrophil, lactoferrin, C3a or CK response in CFS.
note: Women, 15-min step test; n not given

finding: CD5, CD8 and CD11a expression and NK function were lower, and apoptosis higher, in CFS PBMC; a glyconutrient preparation improved these in vitro.
note: In vitro; supplement-company style intervention; n not given

finding: Factor analysis in a San Francisco telephone survey found fatigue of 6+ months clustered with flu-type and cognitive-mood symptoms overlapping CFS criteria.

n: Swedish CFS 57 vs 46 controls; Japanese controls 131
finding: Serum acylcarnitine was low in Swedish CFS patients (p<0.001), as earlier in Japanese patients; also low in hepatitis C but not other diseases.
Patent claiming buprenorphine (lozenge or transdermal gel) as a treatment for CFS and fibromyalgia.
Baseline cortisol was similar, but delta cortisol after 1 microgram ACTH was lower in CFS, and 45% of CFS vs 10% of controls failed a 250 nmol/l cutoff.
After 100 microg ovine CRH, ACTH (P<0.005) and cortisol (P<0.05) responses were blunted in CFS patients without psychiatric illness; basal values equal.
Commentary on the fluoxetine and graded exercise RCT in CFS; no abstract.
Patent describing a culture method to detect 'stealth virus' cytopathic effect.
Antibodies to Yersinia outer membrane proteins did not differ (IgG 27% vs 25%); Y. enterocolitica unlikely to be a major cause.
Commentary noting nonrandomised studies linking neurally mediated hypotension to CFS and that randomised trials were in progress.
Short REM latency correlated with depression within CFS.
9 of 87 CFS patients also met criteria for phosphate diabetes (renal phosphate wasting).
Review arguing a subset of Gulf War illness is CFS/ME or fibromyalgia with possible mycoplasma infection.
Patients with CFS acquired the classically conditioned eyeblink response less well than sedentary controls, with normal sensory responses.
Only a minority of CFS patients were impaired on individual-level neuropsychological testing, and impairment did not match self-reported memory problems or relate to fatigue or depression.
HLA-DR on CD4 and CD8 cells was higher, CD28 on CD8 lower, and bcl-2/bax ratio higher; HLA-DR expression tracked lower SF-36 scores.
Patients with more failing neuropsychological scores reported more inactive days, independent of psychiatric episode or depression.
ACTH, but not cortisol, response to naloxone was blunted in CFS; baseline ACTH and cortisol equal.
Patent claiming AVPR2 gene variants predict CFS susceptibility and treatment with salt or vasopressin antagonists.
Nursing description of the lived experience of CFS.
24-h core body temperature did not differ (CFS 37.04 vs control 37.00 C), with normal circadian rhythm.
CFS patients reported less seasonal variation in energy, mood, appetite, weight and sleep length than controls.
24-h salivary and urinary cortisol did not differ between CFS patients and controls.
Purified CD4 T cells from CFS patients made less interferon-gamma and needed 10- to 20-fold less dexamethasone for 50% inhibition of IL-4 and proliferation.
note: n not given; enhanced glucocorticoid sensitivity at cell level

finding: Patent for a four-herb composition for CFS and AIDS symptoms.
Mean 16-h salivary cortisol was slightly higher in CFS patients than controls (p<0.05), without hypocortisolaemia.
Majority of Japanese CFS patients had low serum DHEA-S.
Discourse-analytic thesis on how ME is constructed in medical, GP and patient talk.
Insurance records show future CFS claimants had more recorded illnesses and claims before diagnosis, with lethargy having the highest odds ratio; authors infer abnormal illness behaviour.
note: Insurance cohort; interpretation not supported by data on mechanism

finding: Retrospective uncontrolled CBT cohort: 35% (6 mo) and 33% (1 yr) reached clinically significant improvement; stressful life events related to outcome.
Actometer activity with hourly fatigue and mood ratings differed from controls in level, diurnal pattern and interrelationships.
Gait analysis showed abnormal symmetry indices and parameter relationships from the first steps, suggested to indicate CNS involvement.
Evening salivary cortisol was lower in CFS than healthy controls (P=0.005) and depressed (P=0.02); morning cortisol lower in CFS without psychiatric disorder (P=0.009).
Urinary free cortisol was lower in CFS than healthy controls and higher in melancholic depression; profile held in CFS with comorbid depression.
Adaptive tasks and coping differed between Parkinson's and CFS; evaluation of tasks predicted quality of life in CFS.
Coronary risk factors, aerobic fitness, BP, lipids and uric acid did not differ from controls, though CFS had lower exercise energy expenditure.
Heart rate variability (HF, LF, LF/HF) did not differ supine or on tilt between CFS and controls.
Apoptotic lymphocytes were higher in CFS (26.6% vs 9.9%) with cell-cycle arrest and higher PKR mRNA and protein.
German review arguing CFS may be a psychosomatic disorder with personality contributions and recommending psychotherapy.
Feeling-of-knowing accuracy was similar to controls despite more reported cognitive symptoms, arguing against a metamemory deficit.
Actometer activity was lower in CFS and MS than healthy subjects, similar between CFS and MS; simple activity questionnaires tracked actometer data.
Post-Lyme patients, but not CFS patients, performed worse than controls on attention, verbal memory, fluency and motor speed; CFS reported more flu-like symptoms.
Home polysomnography showed similar nocturnal sleep time but longer time in bed and more waking after sleep onset in CFS; only a minority had clearly abnormal PSG.
Patent proposing DHEA sulfate as a remedy for CFS.
Physiological evidence of hyperventilation was found more often in CFS than healthy controls, but hyperventilating and non-hyperventilating CFS patients did not differ in severity.
note: Authors call it an epiphenomenon; n not given

finding: At 1 year nearly two thirds reported improvement; poorer outcome predicted by longer illness duration, subjective cognitive difficulty and somatic symptoms, not by anxiety or depression.
CFS, depression and acute infection groups all had more errors, slower reaction times and higher workload than controls; CFS and depression deficits exceeded acute infection.
Sociological review of how CFS emerged as a diagnosis and how definitions affect prevalence.
In English primary care, point prevalence of chronic fatigue was 11.3% and of CFS 2.6% (0.5% excluding psychological disorder).
IgG to HHV-6 in 50%, no IgM; nested PCR of PBMC DNA positive in 40% (1 microgram) to 80% (5 microgram), no viral RNA, arguing against reactivation.
Brain MRI abnormalities in 32% of patients and 28% of controls; white matter hyperintensity prevalence did not differ.
Dutch review of illness attributions as perpetuating factors in CFS.
Pupil dilation after 1% phenylephrine did not differ between CFS and normals (0.931 vs 0.788 mm, p=0.42), so no sympathetic denervation hypersensitivity.

22 of 78 had abnormal tilt; after 8 weeks of sustained-release sodium chloride 11 normalised and improved, 10 still had orthostatic hypotension and had lower plasma renin activity (0.79 vs 1.29 pmol/ml/h in controls).
Dutch review: adolescent CFS prevalence 10-20 per 100,000, unfavourable natural course, treatment aimed at attributions and graded activity.
Estimated CFS prevalence at least 1.1 per 1,000 in four Leiden practices; men:women 1:5.
GP-reported CFS prevalence 112 per 100,000, 81% women.
Perspective arguing CBT is evidence-based for functional somatic complaints, using CFS as example.
A subset of CFS PBMC showed only a 37 kDa or 30 kDa 2-5A-dependent RNase L species rather than 80 and 42 kDa, indicating more complex RNase L dysfunction.
Title only: use of amantadine for CFS; no abstract.
Quality-of-life index scores in CFS were lower than in other chronic illness groups, lowest in health and functioning.
No circulating antimuscle or anti-CNS antibodies were detected in CFS patients or controls.
Most patients held physical explanations, over half also cited stress, and believed activity reduction partly controlled symptoms.

n: 69 CFS no psychiatric vs 58 CFS with vs 38 depressed vs 45 controls
finding: Sleep complaints were similar with or without psychiatric disorder; sleep disturbance was strongly associated with relapse and preceded fatigue in only 20%.
Patients reported low satisfaction with medical support, wanted more information, and often turned to alternative treatment.
Structured interviews found higher current and lifetime psychiatric disorder, notably generalised anxiety disorder and somatisation, in CFS than medical controls.
Live oral polio vaccine did not exacerbate CFS; patients had more poliovirus isolation, earlier proliferative peak, lower T-cell subsets and a trend to lower gamma-interferon.
ACTH, but not cortisol, response to the 5-HT1a agonist ipsapirone was blunted in CFS; baselines equal.
IL-1 receptor antagonist secretion was twofold higher in follicular phase (P=0.023) and soluble IL-1RII higher in both phases (P=0.002) in CFS; menstrual-cycle IL-1 beta variation was absent in CFS.
note: n not given; PBMC secretion in vitro

finding: Patent for diagnosing CFS by PBMC apoptosis, cell-cycle arrest and p68 kinase.
Psychodynamic discussion of CFS/ME with five analytic cases.
CFS subjects showed altered sympathetic and parasympathetic autonomic test results, possibly from deconditioning or post-viral autonomic neuropathy.
Failure to reach 85% of age-predicted maximal HR correlated with impairment; subgroup reaching target showed deconditioning with early anaerobic metabolism.
note: Atlas notes several designs argue against deconditioning

finding: At 10 years 48% of an epidemic neuromyasthenia cohort still met CDC CFS criteria and most had returned to premorbid activity.
Self-reported CFS patients lost 65 work days per year and reported more health care use and iatrogenic illness than general patients.
Under 10% of adults with strictly defined CFS returned to premorbid function; 54-94% of children recovered; poor prognosis linked to age, chronicity, psychiatric comorbidity and physical attribution.
Bioactive TGF-beta was higher in CFS serum than in healthy, depression, SLE and MS groups (P<0.01).
note: Atlas notes serum TGF-beta is largely a platelet artefact; n not given

finding: CFS patients without psychiatric comorbidity were impaired relative to controls on memory, attention and information-processing tests.
CRP, beta2-microglobulin and neopterin were higher in CFS than controls, markers correlated with each other in a subset, and were of limited diagnostic use.
note: Referral clinic; control n not given

finding: 68% of CFS sera had antinuclear antibodies (nuclear envelope, speckled, nucleolar) and 47% anticytoplasmic (vimentin-type); 83% reactive to at least one insoluble antigen.
Physician-based CDC surveillance of unexplained chronic fatigue in four US cities 1989-1993 collecting clinical, laboratory and psychiatric data.
Patent proposing low RNase L inhibitor mRNA or protein in PBMC as a CFS diagnostic.
72% had an infectious-seeming onset but a definite infection was found in 7% of those; stressful events preceded onset in 85% vs 6% of controls.
Review: prevalence about 200 per 100,000 in two studies using the same definition; clusters have better prognosis; no single infectious agent likely.
Conceptual paper on the history of the notion of somatization and its distinction from ME.
Neurocognitive performance did not differ between groups except on one attention and one incidental-memory measure, while psychological distress differed markedly.

Lentivirus-like structures were seen by electron microscopy in lymphocyte cultures from 10 of 17 CFS patients and not matched controls; immunogold and reverse-transcriptase assays failed or were equivocal.
note: Not confirmed; retrovirus claims such as XMRV later failed

finding: Household survey in rural Michigan did not confirm a reported cluster; fatigue features resembled those of generic fatigue.
Polysomnography showed sleep initiation and maintenance disturbance and less stage 4 sleep in CFS, not limited to those with fibromyalgia or psychiatric disorder; REM latency was normal.
35% had a current and 82% a lifetime psychiatric disorder; GHQ below 12 made psychiatric disorder unlikely.
CFS patients scored lower on reaction time and working memory tasks dependent on processing speed, similar to depression; effort on day 1 did not worsen day 2 performance.
CFS subjects complained of reading and concentration problems, but only depressed CFS subjects recalled less text; paired-associate learning did not differ.
Nurses with 6+ months fatigue reported CFS-like symptoms related to perceived accident threat and poor working conditions.
Four years after a sick building outbreak, 10 of 15 fatigued persons were much improved or fatigue free; 2 of 5 with CFS stayed severely impaired.

No differences in white cell counts, immune complexes, complement, immunoglobulins, delayed hypersensitivity, NK function or proliferation; marginal differences in cytokines and surface markers, larger when subgrouped by onset or symptom state.
note: Rigorously defined cases; n not given

finding: T-cell subsets, activation and naive/memory proportions did not differ from controls; NK cells and CD11b+ CD8 cells were higher; immune measures did not change with treatment or predict response.
note: Authors could not replicate immune activation

finding: Spontaneous TNF-alpha (lymphocytes) and IL-6 (monocytes and lymphocytes, also mRNA) were higher and spontaneous IL-10 lower in CFS than matched controls.
CFS criteria symptoms were more common than expected in patients with other unexplained chronic fatigue.
CSF homocysteine was raised in all 12 women meeting both fibromyalgia and CFS criteria and correlated with fatigability; CSF B12 low-normal.
note: No control group in abstract; small

n: 15 CFS vs 15 MS vs 14 depression vs 15 controls
finding: PASAT performance was lower in CFS and depression than controls, but practice effects were not blunted, so fatigue did not universally impair performance.
Serum IGF-1 (somatomedin C) was higher in CFS than controls (255.3 vs 211.9, P=0.01), unlike fibromyalgia.
note: Atlas notes conflicting reports on IGF-1

finding: Sudden-onset CFS had less psychiatric comorbidity and worse memory, gradual onset more psychiatric disease; both had reduced information processing versus controls.
Echinacea and ginseng extracts increased NK activity and ADCC of PBMC from healthy, CFS and AIDS subjects in vitro.
Patent for diagnosing CFS by PBMC p68 kinase activity, apoptosis and cell-cycle analysis.
Paper arguing that chronic low-dose organophosphate exposure may cause a CFS-like syndrome in farmers.
Vagal power was lower in CFS during treadmill walking and in one rest period, and declined after walking, with no group differences in heart rate, VO2 or ventilation.
Post-exercise facilitation of motor evoked potentials was 126% of baseline in CFS vs 218% in controls and 155% in depression.
IgG subclass levels did not show significant deficiencies in CFS versus blood-donor controls or a prospective frozen cohort.
Prolactin response to buspirone was higher in 11 male CFS patients, with more nausea; GH response did not differ.
After a presumed viral illness, chronic fatigue was associated with psychosocial morbidity and avoidance coping; CFS cases (n=23) had little excess psychiatric disorder.
Clinic report on vitamin C infusions with DHEA and antibiotics in patients with CFS-like chronic pneumonia in Nagoya.
Patent for diagnosing CFS by low RNase L inhibitor mRNA in PBMC.
About 52% of CFS sera reacted with nuclear envelope antigens, with IgG immunoprecipitating lamin B1.
CFS patients showed psychomotor slowing, impaired attention, slower learning and impaired delayed recall, with high within-group variability.
SF-36 had excellent reliability in CFS and showed a consistent pattern of lower physical, role and social functioning scores in CFS and other fatigue groups than healthy controls.
Health needs assessment for ME in Wakefield concluded there were no proven services to purchase and prevalence estimates varied widely.
CFS patients differed from controls mainly on learning and memory tests, independent of psychiatric symptoms or psychoactive medication.
Seroprevalence and titres to 13 viruses (HSV, rubella, adenovirus, HHV-6, EBV, CMV, Coxsackie B) were not consistently different from controls in CF, CFS, acute-onset or febrile subsets.
Disability and health-care use were similar across chronic fatigue, CFS, FM and CFS+FM groups; unemployment ranged 26-51%.

n: 223 CFS vs 2,474 population vs disease groups
finding: SF-36 scores in CFS were far below the general population and below most disease groups except depression.
Children with CFS and their parents underestimated activity measured by 3-day ambulatory monitors relative to healthy controls.
Czech review of endocrine disease in the differential diagnosis of CFS, including autoimmune polyglandular syndrome and HPA disorders.
CFS patients were selectively impaired on auditory but not visual paced serial addition, unlike MS patients.
note: Half of each group per task

finding: Chronic fatigue was associated with current psychiatric disorder (60% vs 19%); most CFS cases also had current psychiatric disorder.
High-frequency auditory brainstem responses were abnormal in 10 of 21 suspected CFS patients; prolonged stapedial reflex decay test combined with ABR matched clinical diagnosis in 81.8%.
People attributing fatigue to ME were more fatigued and handicapped at 18 months but less psychologically distressed than those attributing to psychological or social causes.
Core temperature rhythm and melatonin onset did not differ, but their normal correlation was absent in CFS.
MS and CFS patients had similar fatigue severity and were less active than healthy subjects; CFS had higher somatization scores.
Japanese hospital prevalence of CFS was 0.85 per 100,000 and incidence 0.46 per 100,000 person-years; 14.8% were post-infectious.
VO2 max was lower in CFS-MAX than controls (28.1 vs 32.1 mL/kg/min, P=0.05), RPE higher at equal workloads, and a single maximal test did not cause major symptom exacerbation.
CFS Beck Depression Inventory profile resembled depression on mood and vegetative items but had fewer self-reproach and more somatic items than depression.
A urinary metabolite (CFSUM1) and beta-alanine were more abundant in CFS and correlated with symptom indices; severe fatigue was the symptom best matched by CFSUM1.
note: Unidentified compound; no replication known; non-CFS comparison group

finding: Survey of CFS patients found preference for self-help, social support and advocacy services.
CANTAB showed impaired spatial span, spatial working memory and word-association learning in CFS, with normal planning and pattern recognition.
At 18 months 3% reported complete recovery and 17% improvement; predictors were sense of control, lower fatigue, shorter duration and fewer physical attributions.
One third of CFS patients with sicca symptoms fulfilled Sjogren's syndrome criteria but were seronegative.
Maximal post-exercise PCr resynthesis rate (Vmax) in calf was lower in CFS (39.6 vs 53.8 mmol/L/min) and did not fall further 2 days after a maximal treadmill test.
Cases were more likely than matched controls to have exercised regularly before onset (67% vs 40%, OR 3.4); female cases more often nulliparous; premorbid depression and allergy similar.
note: Abstract truncated; cytokine results not shown

finding: Five days of night shift raised basal ACTH, lowered cortisol and blunted the ACTH response to CRH, mimicking CFS HPA findings; authors suggest CFS HPA changes may reflect disrupted sleep.
Patent for NADH and NADPH as CFS treatment, claiming improved strength and symptoms.
GC-MS of first-morning urine separated CFS from non-CFS (P<0.004): higher CFSUM1, tyrosine, beta-alanine, aconitic and succinic acid; lower alanine and glutamate.
Pain thresholds were lower in muscle but normal in skin in 21 CFS patients; quadriceps biopsies in 9 showed sarcomere and mitochondrial abnormalities and raised mtDNA 4977 bp deletion.
German guidance on expert medical assessment of CFS for disability.
No enteroviral RNA was found by RT-PCR in muscle from 34 CFS patients; muscle RNA/DNA ratio and mitochondrial enzyme activities were generally reduced.
Serum IGF-I and IGFBP-3 did not differ between any patient group and controls.
German commentary on CFS in insurance medicine, recommending use of the Kaplan 1988 definition and limiting tests.
GHQ and BDI performed poorly as screeners of psychiatric morbidity in CFS.
Muscle fatigue index was higher in MS (34.2%) than in CFS (27.5%) and controls (23.6%).
CFS patients had slower cognitive and motor processing and lower positive affect than published norms; sustained attention was not impaired.
note: Embedded in terfenadine/placebo trial; no concurrent controls

finding: CD11b on CD8 cells was lower; CD38 and HLA-DR increases were not confirmed; apoptosis and circulating cytokines did not differ; endotoxin-stimulated TNF-alpha and IL-1 beta were lower; none correlated with fatigue.
Essay arguing Holmes-defined CFS does not exist and corresponds to neurocirculatory asthenia.
Serum eosinophil cationic protein was higher in CFS (18.0 vs 7.3 ug/l, P<0.01) and 77% of CFS patients were RAST positive.
Neuroendocrine challenge studies found augmented prolactin responses to buspirone in CFS, evidence of altered serotonergic and HPA function.

n: 42 CFS vs 18 MS vs 21 depression vs 32 healthy
finding: Diagnosed somatization disorder rates in CFS changed dramatically depending on whether symptoms were attributed to psychiatric or physical causes; few met strict criteria.
MMPI scores were elevated on 8 of 9 clinical scales in CFS; EBV early antigen titres were higher in CFS and linked to symptom burden.
No enterovirus was found by faecal isolation, serum-CSF antibody tests or muscle PCR in 34 Swedish CFS patients.
Minor-criteria symptoms including myalgia, post-exertional malaise, headache and infectious-type symptoms distinguished fatigued patients from healthy and MS/depression comparison groups.
MCS, CS and CFS groups all had more psychiatric disorder and unexplained symptoms than controls; 61% of CFS had no Axis I diagnosis.
Referral-clinic CFS cases had higher social class and physical attributions, higher fatigue and impairment, but female excess was not a selection effect.
CFS had intermediate personality pathology scores between depression and healthy controls, mostly accounted for by concurrent depression.
Short report suggesting Borna disease virus infection in Japanese CFS patients.

n: 24 vs 24 pilot; 67 ME/CFS and 40 normals total
finding: HMPAO SPET showed brainstem hypoperfusion in ME/CFS (0.72 vs 0.80, p<0.0001), lower than in depressed patients (0.71 vs 0.77) and with generalised reduced brain perfusion.

finding: Sickness Impact Profile showed markedly impaired quality of life in CFS, especially social functioning.

CFS patients without prior psychiatric problems resembled mild MS more than depression on mood and psychiatric measures.

finding: Adolescent girls with CFS had more somatic complaints, and more internalising symptoms than cancer controls, without family function differences.
